Cyber Attack Disrupts Power Grid and Telecoms Across Greece

ATHENS – A widespread cyber attack targeting Greece's national infrastructure has caused major disruption to electricity and telecommunications networks across the country, with significant knock-on effects for businesses, transportation, and daily life.

The incident, which began early Wednesday morning, has resulted in rolling blackouts in Athens, Thessaloniki, and several regional centres. According to the Ministry of Digital Governance, the attack compromised control systems operated by the Hellenic Power Authority and affected the interconnected networks of major telecommunications provider Ellinet.

"Authorities are working around the clock to restore full functionality and ensure the safety of our critical systems," said Deputy Minister for Civil Protection Giorgos Koulidis at an emergency press briefing. "At this time, we advise all citizens to limit non-essential electricity use and avoid unnecessary travel."

Mobile phone and internet services have been intermittent, with outages reported in the Peloponnese, Crete, and several Aegean islands. Payment processing networks have also experienced delays, with retailers and supermarkets in Athens’ city centre reporting card terminals repeatedly failing.

The Athens Chamber of Commerce and Industry estimated that retail transactions have dropped by as much as 40 percent since the disruptions began. "This is the most serious infrastructure incident Greece has faced in many years," said chamber president Spiros Demetriou. "Small businesses are particularly vulnerable to these kinds of shocks."

At Piraeus Port, Greece’s largest, container handling slowed to a crawl as customs systems went offline. The Hellenic Shipping Union reported delays in vessel departures and warned of potential backlogs if the situation persists.

Cybersecurity analysts from the National Technical University of Athens said the attack bore hallmarks of a coordinated ransomware campaign but stressed that investigations remain ongoing. "This incident highlights the urgent need for investment in cyber resilience across all sectors," said Professor Eleni Markou.

As the response unfolds, officials urge the public to remain calm and follow guidance from authorities. Further updates are expected throughout the day.
